title: PT-4348: Fix the toolbar sync button's startup state, naming, and cancel

reviews.author: katherinejensen00
reviews.bodyText:
This is careful, unusually well-evidenced work — the deviation from the ticket on lastRequestedProjectIds was the right call, the optional-field strategy is sound, and ADR-0014 is more honest about its own limits than most ADRs ever are. But the seeding that is the PR's headline fix does not survive the case it was built for: on a cold start getSyncState doesn't fail fast, it burns ~9 seconds of RPC retries and then gives up permanently with no re-seed, so the status is wrong for exactly the startup scenario the seed exists to fix. Alongside that, the status still reports a failed or user-cancelled sync as "Synced" with a green check, and the popover half of the new test suite may not be executing at all. Those three are worth resolving before merge; the rest are smaller. @katherinejensen00 reviewed 11 files and all commit messages, and made 31 comments. This branch adds ADR-0014 on top of PT-3954's unmerged ADR-0013, while pt-4337-analytics-abstraction-layer adds a different ADR-0013 ("Analytics abstraction layer hosted in extension-host") — I confirmed that directly. Whichever merges second leaves main with two ## ADR-0013 headings, and the append-only convention means nothing catches it at merge time.

Confirmed your finding independently — origin/main tops out at ADR-0012, and pt-4337 does add a
different ADR-0013.
I can't fix another branch's collision from here, so I did the part that's in scope: the log's
"How to use it" now documents that numbers are claimed at MERGE, not at write, with the
instruction that whoever merges second re-reads the last heading on main and renumbers.
⚠️ This one still needs a human at merge time: if pt-4337 lands first, ADR-0013/0014 on this
branch need renumbering before this merges. Nothing automated will catch it. Flagging it here
rather than marking it resolved.

assets/localization/en.json line 483 at r1 (raw file):
Previously, katherinejensen00 wrote…
NIT 22. [Low] The two new interpolated strings have plural and bidi problems
assets/localization/en.json:483 · "Syncing {count} projects" bakes in an English plural; there's no Intl.PluralRules or i18next plural machinery anywhere in the repo, so Slavic/Arabic paucal forms are unproducible. And :482 interpolates an arbitrary-script project name into a directional sentence with no  isolation — combined with truncate, the visible fragment of an RTL name can differ from the intended one.

Split outcome — bidi fixed, plural deferred.
Bidi: interpolated project names are now wrapped in U+2068 / U+2069 (FIRST STRONG ISOLATE /
POP DIRECTIONAL ISOLATE). Used the character-level form rather than  because the result is
a plain string for a button label, not markup. There's a test using an Arabic name.
Plural: deferred, and you're right about why — no Intl.PluralRules or i18next plural machinery
exists anywhere in the repo, so Slavic/Arabic paucal forms are genuinely unproducible today.
Nothing this PR can add short of introducing plural infrastructure, which is a platform-level
change well outside this ticket. "Syncing {count} projects" keeps its baked-in English plural
for now.
Flagging rather than resolving, in case you want it tracked as its own platform gap.

src/@types/paratext-bible-send-receive/index.d.ts line 515 at r1 (raw file):

During a blocking scheduled sync in Simple mode both render at once: two live regions, two Cancel buttons with different labels, neither aware the other was clicked.

You're right, and I'd only documented the C# toast — the sync-blocked-banner overlap was a
genuine gap in the ADR.
Documented rather than merged, deliberately. The two answer different questions: the banner
explains why the editor is unavailable right now and is modal to that editor; the popover is an
ambient whole-app indicator the user opens on purpose. Merging them would mean a shared
cancel-state service neither currently uses, which felt like the wrong thing to bolt on here.
So: ADR-0014 now records the overlap and the concrete defect (a cancel requested in one surface
still reads as armed in the other), both components cross-reference each other at the cancel
site, and reconciling them via one piece of shared cancel-requested state is a named follow-up.
Happy to pull that forward into this PR if you'd rather not ship the overlap.

Merge verdict
Yes — this can merge, but I'd fix four one-liners first. Not the whole
e cheap ones are genuinely cheap. :115 is one clause, :203 is one word (useState('unknown') — no visible label change, both render %toolbar_sync%), :265 is Date.now() → performance.now(), :358 is normalizeProjectId on both sides of a Map. Four small edits close the "the PR contradicts itself" objection. That's a much better trade than another full round.

Everything else is legitimately follow-up. :166 only bites when upstreame. Reachability is dropping round over round — that's the signal that this is close to done.


Round 4. Head 78124d7. Rounds 1–3 all verified as landed — these are new findings from a deeper sweep, not regressions, and reachability is clearly dropping round over round.
My merge read: four one-line fixes, then ship it. Everything below the Blockers section is follow-up material. I'd rather this merged with a linked ticket than took a fifth round.
Blockers — all small


An empty resultsInfo earns the green check. use-sync-status.hook.ts:115. if (!resultsInfo) return false passes for {} because {} is truthy, and Object.values({}).every(...) is vacuously true, so deriveStatusFromSnapshot returns synced. Reachable for a sync aborted or cancelled before any project produced a result entry: the toolbar shows CircleCheck + "Synced" and the popover says "The last sync finished" for a sync that finished nothing. resultsInfo: [] slips through identically. Fix is one clause — require a non-empty map. The suite covers a missing resultStatus and an unrecognised one, never an empty one.


Project-id casing silently defeats project naming. use-sync-status.hook.ts:358. new Map(metadata.map((m) => [m.id, m])) keys on the raw id and metadataById.get(projectId) reads with the raw sync id, but ids are case-insensitive here. getMetadataForAllProjects returns the project (its filter uses areProjectIdsEqual), but project-lookup.service-model.ts:464-468 states outright that md.id "keeps the casing of whichever factory reported it first" — nondeterministic across Promise.all — while C# canonicalizes to uppercase. So get('ABC123') misses 'abc123', ?? projectId fires, and the toolbar reads "Syncing abc123…" instead of "Syncing HNF…" with nothing logged. That is the PR's headline feature failing silently. use-project-picker-data.hook.ts:326,333 runs normalizeProjectId on both sides of this same lookup; this hook doesn't. Same root cause makes isSameProjectIdSet (:77) read a casing change as a set changeta lookup.
3. The status starts iNo sync is running" for up to 60s. use-sync-status.hook.ts:203. When send/receive is present but getSyncState isn't registered yet, useSendReceiveAvailability answers true and the button rendersStatus('unknown') only runs once the deadline passes. For that whole window status is the initial 'idle' and clicking shows %toolbar_sync_popover_idle% — even
during a live startup 1 of this same file sayround 2's "failed sync shows a green check" — three sites that fix didn't cover.



The cold-start path has a hole the seed retry doesn't cover. The first
event permanently la but the event path has no retry of its own, and the initial state is idle — so during the whole retry window the popover positively asserts "No sync is running," which is the exact claim the hook's own header forbids.
The casing bug is the one I'd fix first. It has nothing to do with sync logic — it silently defeats the PR's headline feature. project-lookup.service-model.ts:464-468 documents in so many words that returned ids keep the casing of whichever factory reported first, and C# canonicalizes to uppercase; use-project-picker-data.hook.ts normalizes both sides for this reason, this hook doesn't.

On verdicts: CONFIRMED means the mechanism is code-mechanical and line-traceable (I re-verified the top three myself against the PR head);
PLAUSIBLE means it turavior I can't checkfrom core — notably #13, which is only decidable from upstream sync-state.ts (does one sync episode claim its project set atomically, or incrementally?). That one is worth settling before merge since the whole cancel re-arm heuristic rests on the answer.
